### T110. Meal Planning Sheet — Rules and Conventions

<!-- TECHNIQUE-TAGS: cody, meal-planning-sheet, planning, staples, difficulty-circle, maintenance-time, hands-on-time, outdoor-marker, sort-order, sauces-block, rubs-block -->
**Tags:** `cody` · `meal-planning-sheet` · `planning` · `staples` · `difficulty-circle` · `maintenance-time` · `hands-on-time` · `outdoor-marker` · `sort-order` · `sauces-block` · `rubs-block`
**Source:** Cody's own instructions, dictated across 2026-09-09 — every rule below is quoted from him or reasoned from a rule he set. Not a cooking technique; a reference for how the [Meal Planning Sheet](../meal-planning-sheet.md) is built and read.
**Used by:** the [Meal Planning Sheet](../meal-planning-sheet.md) — and by whoever edits it next.

**Why this entry exists.** On 2026-09-09 (final) Cody stripped the sheet down to its tables: ***"I don't need all that text. This is a whole lot of text of how to use and yada yada. What I really want is just the table as a reference. We're gonna put the page on the fridge. I'm not trying to print ten pages. Nobody's gonna be reading that gobbledygoop. Sauces — this is the deepest shelf in the cookbook, there's no reason for that. Get rid of all the description text. It's a reference document."*** So the sheet now carries one title line, one legend line, and the tables. **Everything it used to say is here instead, moved verbatim and lightly stitched** — the how-to, the legend in full, the difficulty-circle and maintenance-square rules, the ♨︎ rules, the change notes, the sauces-block commentary, and the group-header notes. Nothing was deleted; it was moved so that none of it prints.

#### The rules added 2026-09-09 (final) — staples, the sauce notation, the filled right column

- **⏰ Every ⭐ Staple recipe carries a *Countdown to dinner* line, as of 2026-09-09.** It sits directly under the recipe's difficulty and time badge and reads the method backward from the moment food hits the table — *T−3 days salt, bag, into the bath · T−1 day into the ice chest · T−4½ hr light the smoker · T−20 min rest and slice* — one stage per ` · `, newest-to-oldest, with the offsets taken only from that entry's own badge and steps (prep, cook, slow cook, and any dry brine, marinade, soak, chill or rest the method states; a *light the smoker/grill* stage on ♨︎ methods where the entry readies the pit). Nothing in it is new content: it is a derived, machine-readable restatement of the entry, so where the entry gives a range the line gives the range, and where the entry never states a timing the line says so and points at Open Questions rather than guessing. **This is what the weekly-planning conversation uses to place calendar events** — "Monday dinner at 7, pulled pork" becomes the salt-it reminder Saturday evening, the rub Sunday morning, the pit Sunday at 10 p.m., and the pull at 6:40 — each one counted back from the dinner time Cody names. All 36 ⭐ Staple Mains and 27 ⭐ Staple Sides carry one; the four sauce links on the chicken-thigh line are sauces and do not.
- **⭐ Staples lead the sheet.** *"The first two categories I want to be Roberts' staple meals: staple main dishes, and then staple sides."* **⭐ Staple Mains** and **⭐ Staple Sides** are the first group in each column of the main table, **⭐ Staple Rubs** is the first row of the rubs block, and **⭐ Staple Sauces** the first row of the sauces block. **A staple line is a copy of the recipe's line in its regular group — same markers, same link — and the regular line stays where it is.** Staples are a curated view on top of the sheet, not a move; nothing leaves Beef or Pork or Vegetables to be a staple. Each staple group sorts by minutes ascending, ❤️ then 👍 breaking ties, like every other group. **Staple Rubs is the default rub**: when a recipe says *your favorite rub*, reach for one of those. **Explicitly not staples, on his say-so:** Jalapeño Poppers (*"is not a staple, sorry"*), and both big-steak lines ([§7.36](736-two-steaks-feed-four.md), [§7.106](7106-big-thick-steakhouse-steaks.md) — *"I'm not sure how that's different… feels a little redundant"*; both stay in Beef and both entries carry the question). Of the four pulled-pork methods only [§6.9 Cody's](69-codys-pulled-pork.md) is a staple; his *"maybe condense"* remark on the other three is logged in [§12](12-recipes-to-document.md). **Six unlinked *(§N — …)* placeholder lines stood in for the recipes he named as staples before their entries existed** — [§6.12](612-sous-vide-chuck-roast-smoker-finished.md), [§6.13](613-beer-can-chicken-codys-tony-chacheres-upright-smoked-chicken.md), [§7.152](7152-gluten-free-fried-shrimp.md), [§5.5](55-salted-sautéed-zucchini-noodle-substitute.md), [§5.64](564-quick-salad-with-homemade-dressing.md) *(the placeholder read §5.65; §5.64 was the next free number)* and [§4.197](4197-lawrys-seasoned-salt-store-bought.md). **All six were written up later on 2026-09-09 (Stage 2) and the lines now carry links and the full marker set**; each also took its line in its regular group.
- **Child sauces read parent + child.** *"You say twenty minutes, fifteen minutes — so is it ten minutes for the base and then if you add another thing it becomes Mornay, twenty minutes total? Unclear. If it's an additional ten minutes, just push plus ten there."* So in the sauces block every sauce built on a parent shows `🟩(10 + 10 min)`: the first number is the parent's own minutes, the second is what the child adds, and the square's color is on the total. The parents: [§4.63 béchamel/velouté](463-sauce-béchamel--sauce-velouté-master-white-sauce.md) at 10; the brown children on [§4.71 Sauce Brune](471-sauce-brune-flour-based-brown-sauce--brown-sauce-1.md) at 35 (or 10 if you start from [§4.73 Jus Lié](473-jus-lié-starch-thickened-brown-sauce--brown-sauce-3.md), the quick base); [§4.9 Hollandaise](49-hollandaise-sauce.md) at 35 under the béarnaise and Choron; [§4.187 Homemade Mayonnaise](4187-homemade-mayonnaise.md) at 10 under the aioli and rouille. The child numbers are the ones each entry's badge already carried — every one of those badges says *plus making the base* — so nothing was re-derived, only made visible. Sauces whose entries build their own base from a roux ([§4.68](468-sauce-au-cari-light-curry-sauce.md), [§4.69](469-sauce-soubise-onion-sauce.md), [§4.70](470-sauce-bâtarde--sauce-au-beurre-mock-hollandaise.md), [§4.52](452-balsamella.md)) are not children and keep a single number.
- **The right column is filled.** *"A large percentage is blank on the right side. If the sides are completely done, start filling it out with other main dishes and label those both as main dishes."* The main table pairs Staple Mains with Staple Sides, then the regular main groups with the regular side groups until the sides run out; a **Mains (cont.) | Mains (cont.)** row follows, and the remaining main groups continue down both columns, each group kept whole in one column and the two columns balanced by line count. The appetizer block keeps its two groups as its two columns. The rubs and sauces blocks are **names and markers only**; every description sentence that used to sit in them is below.

#### The sheet as it read before 2026-09-09 (final) — moved here verbatim

*Everything below is the prose the sheet carried up to that day, in the order it appeared. Rule numbers, "above"/"below" and "this sheet" refer to the sheet as it was then; the tables they describe are still on the [Meal Planning Sheet](../meal-planning-sheet.md), now without this text around them. Two anchors moved with the reorganizations of the same day: [§3](3-darcys-steak.md)'s reverse sear is now the body of that entry (the old §3.D link points at §3), and the Sauces sub-blocks are rows of one table, so their old sub-heading links point at [Sauces](../meal-planning-sheet.md#sauces).*


**Print this and put it on the fridge.** It answers one question — *what are we having?* — and nothing else. Mains run down the left, sides down the right, the way you'd actually plan a dinner.

#### How to use this

1. **Pick one main from the left column.**
2. **Add one or two sides from the right column.** The two columns run independently — a side is not matched to the main sitting next to it. Pick freely.
3. **Anything marked 🍽️ is the whole meal. Skip the right column entirely.** The starch and the vegetable are already in it.
4. **Everything inside a group is sorted by the maintenance-time square, quickest first — ❤️ then 👍 only break ties.** ***Cody's rule of 2026-09-09 (late), and it applies to every group in both columns, to the appetizer block, and to the rub and sauce rows.*** In his words: *"Re-order within each category — the quickest pork main dish would be at the top of the pork category… in time order, least amount of time first."* The ❤️-first rule he set earlier the same day is not withdrawn, just demoted to the tiebreaker, so among equal times the family favorites still come first. A range sorts (and colours) on its low end. **Anything added later gets sorted into place, not appended to the bottom**, and a recipe whose minutes change moves. *(The five pins he named earlier that day — [Sous Vide Chicken](t28-sous-vide-chicken-codys-method.md), [Easy Caulimash](115-easy-caulimash-keto-mashed-potatoes.md), [Southern Fauxtato Salad](114-southern-fauxtato-salad-cauliflower-potato-salad.md), [Brazilian Black Beans](534-brazilian-black-beans-with-bacon-tutu-mineira.md), and the [romaine salad](561-simple-romaine-or-butter-lettuce-salad-with-grana-padano.md) — now take their place by time like everything else, and on their own minutes four of the five sit first in their groups anyway. If he wants a pin back above the sort, say so.)* Two things the sort deliberately leaves alone: the French mother-sauce table, whose order is *the parent first, then its children*, and any sauce row whose first item is marked *(the parent)* — the parent stays first and the rest sort behind it.
5. **Appetizers and dips have their own block** at the bottom, below the main sheet.
6. **A bold label with names after it is a cluster** — one dish a source printed several ways. Pick any version; they are alternatives to each other, not courses.
7. **Seasoning gets two blocks at the bottom, not one.** [Rubs & Seasonings](../meal-planning-sheet.md#rubs--seasonings-by-protein) is mapped to the protein it goes on. [Sauces](../meal-planning-sheet.md#sauces) is its own block, grouped by what a sauce *is* — the French families, wine and brown sauces, butter and emulsions, fish and seafood, barbecue and vinegar, fresh and cold, pasta and tomato. **§4 holds about four sauces for every rub, so they no longer share a strip.**

**You can plan Monday through Friday straight off this page in conversation** — read down the left column, call out five mains, and we'll fill in sides and build the grocery list from each recipe's own shopping list.

**Legend:** **🟢 easy · 🟡 medium · 🔴 hard — the circle before every recipe name is difficulty, and difficulty is technique risk, not effort or time** · ❤️ family favorite · 👍 tried and liked · 🥑 keto / low-carb · 🍽️ the whole meal, no side needed · ♨︎ **outdoor cooking is required by the method** — a smoke phase, a live-fire cook, or something only coals can do · **🟩🟨🟥 maintenance time — the minutes you are actually working on the dish: hands-on time only, nothing that is just waiting** — 🟩 under 45 min · 🟨 45 min–1 hr 15 min · 🟥 over 1 hr 15 min · **†** the figure is Cody's own · `incl. 30 grill` / `incl. 10 sear` — that overhead is already inside the number shown, not on top of it

> 🟢🟡🔴 **The circles, added 2026-09-09 at Cody's request** — *"Before the title — so on pulled pork sandwiches, you would put a green circle, Cody's Pulled Pork Sandwiches. Geoff's Pork Belly, green. Um, yellow circle, red for hard. But do that before the title of each recipe."* **Difficulty leads, the name follows, and every other marker stays where it always was, after the name.** Each circle is read straight off that recipe's own badge line, so the sheet cannot drift from the entries.
>
> 🟩🟨🟥 **The squares, added the same day, are a second and entirely different question: not *is this risky* but *how much of my own time does this cost me?*** Cody wanted it **"after the heart and before any other emoji"** — so the line order is now **circle → name → ❤️/👍 → 🟩/🟨/🟥(minutes) → everything else (🥑, 🍽️, ♨︎)**. **Squares, not a second set of circles, on purpose** — two colored circles in front of one name reads as one marker doubled, not two different questions. 🟢🟡🔴 stays reserved for difficulty; 🟩🟨🟥 is always paired with a `(N min)` figure, which is the tell for which is which even in a black-and-white printout.
>
> **The number is hands-on time, and since Cody's line-by-line review on 2026-09-09 (late) it follows three rules.** The first version of the square was a mechanical Prep + Cook read off each badge; he went through the result line by line and the rule came out tighter.
>
> **Rule 1 — hands-on time only.** *"If you have to bake it in the oven, you don't count baking in the oven, because that's just waiting." · "Soup simmering should not count." · "Just do the prep time."* The square is **the minutes you are actually working** — chopping, mixing, searing, checking, turning, assembling. It excludes every Slow cook stretch (*"I put it in overnight, I don't check it"*) **and every unattended oven bake or stovetop simmer of any length, even under two hours** — a 45-minute simmer you stir twice is not 45 minutes of maintenance. It includes attended cooking: a sear, a stir-fry, wings you check every ten minutes, a roux you cannot leave, a batch of steaks brought to temperature one at a time. **This is deliberately narrower than [CLAUDE.md §3a](../../CLAUDE.md)'s Cook field, which keeps short unattended stretches inside it. The badges on the entries and the [Difficulty & Time Index](../index.md) are unchanged — only this sheet's square uses the narrower definition** — so a square can sit well under its badge's Prep + Cook and both are right; they answer different questions.
>
> **Rule 2 — grill overhead.** *"Overriding anything that I just said: a grill is an extra thirty minutes."* Any **main or appetizer** cooked on the grill or smoker — the ♨︎ lines — carries **+30 min** for lighting and readying the pit, shown as `incl. 30 grill` inside its number. **Grilled sides get none** — *"I'm only gonna be doing grilled sides while I'm doing a grilled meat. I don't have to prep the grill for a side"* — and neither do the rubs and sauces that are made on a pit, which ride along the same way. **A pan-seared finish gets +10, not +30** — *"if you're searing, that takes an extra ten minutes"* — applied to the sous vide dishes that finish in a skillet, shown as `incl. 10 sear`. **Leftovers get neither: they are reheated, never grilled.**
>
> **Rule 3 — Cody's own figures override everything.** A **†** after the minutes means the number is his, given line by line on 2026-09-09. His number is the whole number — **no overhead is added on top of it**, and it is not re-derived. Where his figure is a range the range is shown, and it sorts and colours on its low end. **Buckets, Cody's own numbers:** 🟩 under 45 min · 🟨 45 min to 1 hr 15 min · 🟥 over 1 hr 15 min. **Store-bought products with no badge to read — [§4.87 Cavender's](487-cavenders-all-purpose-greek-seasoning-store-bought.md), [§4.88 Vegeta](488-vegeta-store-bought-croatian-all-purpose-seasoning.md), and since 2026-09-09 (Stage 2) [§4.197 Lawry's Seasoned Salt](4197-lawrys-seasoned-salt-store-bought.md) — carry no time marker**, the same treatment they already get for the difficulty circle: there is nothing to make, so nothing to time, and they sort as zero minutes. **[§4.108 Meathead's Memphis Dust](4108-meatheads-memphis-dust.md) does carry a normal marker** despite the standing pantry stash noted in [CLAUDE.md §6](../../CLAUDE.md) — that note is about skipping it on a grocery list, not about how long it takes to mix.
>

overhead to the ♨︎ mains and appetizers and sear overhead to the sous vide dishes that finish in a skillet — on top of the old Prep + Cook numbers. **This pass then re-read every remaining square (one link each way came off, one came on in the tacos note) — and **432 recipe links before, 432 after, the same 432**; the re-sort moved lines, it removed none. Section pointers (like [T. Cooking Techniques & Tips](../index.md)) and the two store-bought items above still correctly carry no marker.
>
> **What the circle answers, and why it is worth the ink: *does this need my attention?*** It is **technique risk, not time** — [CLAUDE.md §3a](../../CLAUDE.md)'s rule, the same one the [Difficulty & Time Index](../index.md) runs on. **A long cook is not a hard one.** An eight-hour crock pot is **🟢** because not one of those eight hours can go wrong; a fifteen-minute dark roux is **🔴** because it goes from perfect to burnt while you answer the door. That is exactly the split a planning sheet should surface: **the circle tells you whether a dish needs you standing over it, and the time fields in the [Difficulty & Time Index](../index.md) tell you whether it needs a place on your calendar.** They are different questions and this page should never conflate them — [§1 Cody's Pho](1-codys-pho.md) is two days long and 🟢.
>
> **Three kinds of line deliberately carry no circle.** **Group headers** (**🥩 Beef & Venison**, **🥕 Vegetables**) and **cluster labels** (**Crawfish Bisque:**, **Brisket:**) are not recipes — but every recipe *inside* a cluster carries its own, because the versions genuinely differ: the three crawfish bisques come out **🔴 · 🟡 · 🟡**. **Section pointers** — [T. Cooking Techniques & Tips](../index.md), [§4](4-rubs-seasonings-sauces--condiments.md), the [Fish & seafood sauces](../meal-planning-sheet.md#sauces) pointer on the broiled fish line — point at a place, not a method. And the **No-Cook items with no entry** (cottage cheese, sliced tomatoes, avocado, applesauce) have no badge to read.
>
> **Three named entries have no circle on purpose, and that is not an oversight: [§4.88 Vegeta](488-vegeta-store-bought-croatian-all-purpose-seasoning.md) ❤️, [§4.87 Cavender's Greek Seasoning](487-cavenders-all-purpose-greek-seasoning-store-bought.md) ❤️, and [§4.197 Lawry's Seasoned Salt](4197-lawrys-seasoned-salt-store-bought.md) ❤️ (added 2026-09-09, Stage 2).** They are **store-bought products rather than recipes** — there is nothing to make, so they carry no badge anywhere in this cookbook and none was invented for them here. A rating would have had to be made up, and a made-up circle on a planning sheet is worse than a blank one.
>
> **[§3 Darcy's Steak](3-darcys-steak.md) is the one line with two methods behind it, and both land on 🟢 — on Cody's call, 2026-09-09.** The sous vide body (Steps 1–9) and its [§3.D stovetop reverse sear](3-darcys-steak.md) sat at 🟡 for the sear with no doneness cushion; he settled it: *"I think easy is perfect if they follow the directions."* The entry now argues it his way — the risk exists only if you skip the directions, and the directions (pat dry, oil, a short timed sear, pull early) are the whole protection. **So the sheet's 🟢 is right whichever way you cook it**, and no second circle is needed.
>
> **This supersedes the old arrangement in the [Sauces](../meal-planning-sheet.md#sauces) block**, where only the three 🔴 sauces were flagged and everything else went unmarked. Cody said *each recipe*, and a sauce is a recipe — so all 98 of them now carry their rating, and the three standalone 🔴 marks that used to trail those names came off, since the circle in front now says it.

> ♨︎ **What the ♨︎ means, added 2026-09-09 at Cody's request** — *"can you put a little grill icon in anything that typically involves the grill? Anything that involves the grill or the smoker, or any kind of outdoor cooking."* **So it covers all of it: the grill, the smoker, the Big Green Egg, a charcoal chimney, a kamado, a rotisserie, and frying outdoors on a grill's side burner.**
>
> **📌 He narrowed it the same day, and the narrower rule is the one in force.** In his words: *"Sous vide brisket — some of that stuff can be pan seared, it doesn't have to be grilled. All the sous vide stuff… I guess smoked sous vide steak has to be grilled, that's a different story. But a lot of this can be pan seared if it's sous vided."* **So ♨︎ now means outdoor cooking is *required by the method* — a smoke phase, a live-fire cook, or a technique that only works over coals. If the only outdoor element is a final sear that a screaming-hot cast-iron pan could do just as well, the marker comes off.** A sear is a sear; the fire is interchangeable there in a way a smoke phase never is. **The test applied to every single line: strip the outdoor equipment away — does the dish stop existing?** If it does, the marker stays. If it doesn't, it goes.
>
> **Every marked line was re-read against that rule on 2026-09-09, and the count moved from 101 markers to 100.** **One came off, and it is precisely the case the new rule was written for: [§3 Darcy's Steak](3-darcys-steak.md).** It cooks in a water bath and meets fire only at the very end, over a charcoal chimney — and its own **[§3.D stovetop reverse sear](3-darcys-steak.md)** is that same steak, same rub, same 129°F, with no charcoal anywhere in it. The chimney is a hotter sear than a pan and the entry says so; it is still only a sear. **[§T28 Sous Vide Chicken](t28-sous-vide-chicken-codys-method.md) is the reference for what "sear, not grill" looks like** — blazing cast iron, 30 to 45 seconds a side — and it has correctly never carried the marker. Neither does its family-sized recipe, **[§7.151 Sous Vide Chicken Thighs](7151-sous-vide-chicken-thighs-for-the-family-seared.md)**.
>
> **Four sous vide dishes kept the marker, and not one of them kept it for the sear.** **[§7.131 Smoked Sous-Vide Steak](7131-smoked-sous-vide-steak.md)** keeps it on Cody's own say-so — *"smoked sous vide steak has to be grilled, that's a different story"* — and the page backs him up: a **30-minute smoke** sits between the bath and the sear, while the sear itself is explicitly allowed in a pan or under a broiler. **[§6.10 Sous Vide Brisket](610-sous-vide-brisket-richies-method.md)** keeps it because what follows the bath is **four hours at 225°F over pecan** — a smoke phase, not a sear. The *hot browning* on the Egg after that **is** the sear, and that part could be done in a pan; the four hours could not. Its smoked salt ([§4.195](4195-codys-smoked-salt.md)) is load-bearing in the recipe besides, and that is made on a pit too. **[§7.149 The Ultimate Prime Rib Roast](7149-the-ultimate-prime-rib-roast.md)** keeps it for a **90-minute pellet smoke at 165°F** that happens *before* the bath; its finishing sear could be a pan. **[§7.59 Mediterranean Pork Tenderloin Platter](759-mediterranean-pork-tenderloin-platter-vegeta-rubbed-sous-vide--seared.md)** keeps it even though **its pork already sears in cast iron** — the fire is there for the vegetables and the naan, which is a cook over live fire rather than a sear.
>
> **A grill reverse sear keeps the marker, because the fire does both stages.** [§7.106 Big, Thick Steakhouse Steaks](7106-big-thick-steakhouse-steaks.md), [§7.108 Santa Maria Tri-Tip](7108-santa-maria-tri-tip.md), [§7.109 Chateaubriand](7109-chateaubriand-with-compound-butter.md), [§7.114 Prime Rib](7114-prime-rib.md) and [§7.115 Steakhouse Steakburgers](7115-the-great-american-steakhouse-steakburger.md) all warm the meat in a 225°F indirect zone and *then* sear it over the coals. The outdoor element there is the whole cook, not just the finish, so the new rule doesn't reach them.
>
> **Two lines are genuinely borderline, and they say so here rather than quietly losing the marker.** **[§7.9 Caveman Chicken Wings](79-caveman-chicken-wings.md)** keeps it, but read the entry before you plan around it: Cody's own method is **oven or Big Green Egg, both at 400°F**, and the single hickory chunk belongs to the Egg alone — so the fire is what makes them *smoky*, not what makes them *wings*. *(The name describes the whole uncut wing with the drumette attached, not the cooking — that was settled on the entry 2026-09-08.)* **[§9.21 Dressed-Up Hummus with Garlic Naan](921-dressed-up-hummus-with-garlic-naan.md)** keeps it because grilling the naan is the only cooking anywhere in the entry and the grill is Cody's own instruction — though its step names a **375°F oven** as the alternative in the same breath.
>
> **The icon reflects the recipe as written, not what is possible.** That distinction is still doing most of the work, because half the meat in this book *could* be cooked outside. **A steak the recipe cooks in cast iron gets no ♨︎ even though you could obviously grill it.** **Where a recipe's own method puts the actual cooking outside and offers an indoor fallback, it keeps the ♨︎** — [§4.113 Citrus Salt and Pepper](4113-citrus-salt-and-pepper.md) dehydrates its citrus on a grill topper and says an oven "works too," and [§7.123 Kufte Kebabs](7123-kufte-kebabs.md) grills over hot coals with a cast-iron alternative printed underneath it. **Where the method is indoors and merely permits a grill, it gets nothing** — [§15.8 Skillet Cornbread](158-old-fashioned-skillet-cornbread-and-hush-puppies.md) preheats an oven to 400°F "or the grill's indirect side," and it stays unmarked.
>
> **And a mention of smoke is not an outdoor cook.** Smoked paprika, smoked salt, smoked sausage, liquid smoke, and a store-bought smoked salmon all show up in dishes cooked entirely indoors — [§8.3 Chicken and Andouille Gumbo](83-chicken-and-andouille-smoked-sausage-gumbo.md) is a stovetop pot with smoked sausage in it, and [§5.34 Brazilian Black Beans](534-brazilian-black-beans-with-bacon-tutu-mineira.md) says so itself: *no grill involved at all, despite the book it comes from.* **Every marked line here was read in full before it was marked, and read again on 2026-09-09 before it was allowed to keep the mark** — nothing here was matched on a word. **This is a planning-sheet affordance only** — the ♨︎ is not added to entry headings, the [Table of Contents](../index.md), or either ratings index.

**A dish that brings its own sauce or topping is one line here, sauce included.** [§7.119 Big Bob Gibson's Chicken in 'Bama White Sauce](7119-big-bob-gibsons-chicken-in-bama-white-sauce.md) is one main — the white sauce is part of the dish, not a separate pick. Same with the avocado salsa on [§7.150](7150-grilled-salmon-with-avocado-salsa.md) and the dipping sauce on [§9.32](932-coconut-beer-shrimp-with-sweet-and-tangy-dipping-sauce.md). You will not find any of those three sauces anywhere else on this sheet, including in the [Sauces](../meal-planning-sheet.md#sauces) block.

**Everything cookable is on this page, and that is the point.** A planning sheet you cannot plan a whole week from is worse than useless — it sends you back to the [Table of Contents](../index.md), and once that happens you stop using the sheet at all. So every written-up recipe in [§1](1-codys-pho.md)–[§3](3-darcys-steak.md), [§5](5-vegetables--sides.md)–[§11](11-southern-keto-baking--sides.md) and [§15](15-breads.md) is here. **Three things are left off, and only these three:** **placeholders** — the ○ entries in the Table of Contents, which have no method written down yet, so there is nothing to cook; **[§4](4-rubs-seasonings-sauces--condiments.md)**, whose rubs and sauces get their own two blocks at the bottom of this sheet; and **[§14 Desserts](14-desserts.md)**, per the closing note below.

**Where one source printed several versions of the same dish, all of them are here — clustered onto a single line** under a shared bold label, versions separated by `·`: the crawfish bisques, the courtbouillons, the briskets, the waterfowl gumbos, the turtle soups, the crawfish pies, Raichlen's six world beef kebabs. That keeps the page scannable without dropping anything. **Nothing is omitted for being a variation.**

It is not a new *dish* — it is the ❤️ placeholder that has sat in §5 since the beginning, finally written up, so it arrives with its favorite mark already earned and sorts to the top of the group on rule 4.
> - **And [§5.7 Brussels Sprouts](57-brussels-sprouts.md) ❤️ joined 🥕 Vegetables later on 2026-09-09** — the second ❤️ placeholder from the top of §5 written up that day, after §5.2. Sorted into the group on rule 4 at **🟩(22 min)** — 10 of trimming and halving plus a 12-minute attended sauté, no grill overhead because it is a stovetop side — between the 20-minute lines and the 25s. **Three fats, one line:** bacon grease, tallow, or butter are variations inside the entry, not three sheet lines.
> - **Six 👍 marks were missing from this sheet** that the [Family Ratings Index](../index.md) already carried — [§5.11](511-sweet-potato-casserole.md), [§5.12](512-southern-cornbread-stuffing.md), [§5.13](513-north-carolina-coleslaw.md), [§5.14](514-grilled-corn.md), [§7.33](733-grilled-stuffed-chicken-breasts.md), and [§11.3](113-keto-skillet-cornbread.md). They are on now. **The sort is only as good as the marks**, so those had to be right before it would mean anything.

> **📌 Later still on 2026-09-09, he reviewed every square line by line and rebuilt the page around the result** — the three rules above, the time-first sort in rule 4, and seven structural changes. **Nothing was removed to do it.**
>
> - **A new 🍱 Leftovers group closes the mains column.** *"We should have leftovers as a thing… you could use leftovers as a real meal for two nights in a row doing it differently."* Sliced brisket reheated in the sous vide, pulled pork sandwiches and street tacos, kebabs, leftover chili into [§8.1 Chili Mac](81-chili-mac.md) (and [§8.47 Frito Pie](847-frito-pie.md) ❤️, written up in Stage C the same day), and [§7.146](7146-pho-with-leftover-brisket-and-smoked-bone-broth.md) — which reads **Pho with Leftover Beef** here now, on his note that he sous vides two or three chuck roasts at a time and reuses them for pho. **No line in that group carries ♨︎** — *"all leftovers does not need the grill."* **The old "Sliced Smoked Brisket" line confused him** (*"I don't understand that… there's smoked brisket"*), so [§6.1](61-smoked-brisket.md) now reads plain **Smoked Brisket** — the cook, 60–90 min on his figure — and the sliced-leftover idea lives in Leftovers.

He doubts both times (*"cherry chutney — how long does that take? and the pine nut salad? I'm not convinced"*); they are on the re-read list.

I want it like that"*); [§7.15](715-pauls-jambalaya.md) is *Paul's Jambalaya*, apostrophe and all, and it is **🟢 now on his call, 30 min** (*"prep time takes thirty minutes; baking is waiting"*) — the one change here that did reach an entry's badge; and §7.146 is *Pho with Leftover Beef*, above.

You figure it out."* Settled under [CLAUDE.md §3d](../../CLAUDE.md): a butt is a roast and ribs are not, so his 45 sits on the butt as a † figure with that reading labeled on the line, and the ribs got the same hands-on re-read as everything else.**

#### Appetizers & Dips — block notes

Their own block, because they aren't a main and they aren't a side — they're what goes out before dinner.

#### Rubs & Seasonings, by Protein — block notes

**The dry side of the pantry** — rubs, dry seasonings, brines and injections, mapped to the protein they go on. **Sauces have their own block, right below this one.** These are the **general-purpose** ones you'd freely reach for on any piece of meat. **A rub that belongs to one specific recipe is not here**; it stays with its dish — the Cowboy Java rub is part of [§7.100](7100-pork-tenderloin-with-cowboy-java-rub.md), not a separate pick. All 31 live in [§4](4-rubs-seasonings-sauces--condiments.md).

#### Sauces — block notes

**This is the deepest shelf in the cookbook, and it had been getting one line while the rubs got five.** [§4](4-rubs-seasonings-sauces--condiments.md) holds roughly **126 sauces against 31 rubs** — the entire *Mastering the Art of French Cooking* sauce chapter, the Prudhomme seafood sauces, the regional barbecue sauces, and a long bench of fresh and cold ones. **They are grouped below by what a sauce *is* and what it goes on**, not by which book it came out of.

**Every sauce here now carries its own difficulty circle in front of the name, 🟢 / 🟡 / 🔴 — added 2026-09-09, and it replaces the old arrangement where only the three 🔴 ones were flagged.** Cody's instruction was *each recipe*, and a sauce is a recipe. **🔴 still means what it meant: that sauce can break on you** — worth knowing before you pick it on a Tuesday — but now a 🟢 tells you the opposite just as plainly, which the blank never did. ❤️ is a family favorite, same as everywhere else on this sheet.

**The same rule as the rubs applies here.** A sauce that a single dish builds in stays with that dish and is not a separate pick — the Alabama white sauce is part of [§7.119](7119-big-bob-gibsons-chicken-in-bama-white-sauce.md), the avocado salsa part of [§7.150](7150-grilled-salmon-with-avocado-salsa.md), the sweet-and-tangy dip part of [§9.32](932-coconut-beer-shrimp-with-sweet-and-tangy-dipping-sauce.md). You will not find those three anywhere on this sheet.

**But the rule is about what a recipe *builds in*, not about what a recipe *mentions* — and three items came back onto the sheet on 2026-09-09 because they had failed that test the wrong way**, the same mistake already corrected once for [§4.1 Darcy's Steak Rub](41-darcys-steak-rub.md). [§4.109 Simon & Garfunkel Rub](4109-simon--garfunkel-rub.md) is *referenced* by [§7.118](7118-simon--garfunkel-chicken.md), not built into it. [§4.23 Remoulade Sauce](423-remoulade-sauce.md) ❤️ is used by [§9.9](99-shrimp-remoulade.md) **and** [§9.10](910-crabmeat-avery.md). And [§4.18 Lemon Butter Sauce](418-lemon-butter-sauce.md) is claimed by no dish at all — its own source line says *serve this over fish, veal, beef steaks, or lamb chops*, and the asparagus recipes that sound like they own it use a different butter, [§4.56](456-canal-house-lemon-butter.md).

**And this is still a planning sheet, so it is curated — 98 of the roughly 126 are named here.** Where a source printed several near-identical versions of one sauce — seven vinaigrettes, four herb salsas, four pestos, three Carolina vinegar sauces, two Lexington dips — **the parent is named and the rest are pointed at in the note under its group. [§4](4-rubs-seasonings-sauces--condiments.md) holds the complete list.**

**The French mother sauces & their children.**

**These are a system, not a list.** One master white sauce and one master brown sauce, each turned into a dozen others by adding a single thing — cheese, tomato, onion, mustard, wine, mushrooms. Learn the two parents and the children come nearly free. **[§T24 The French Sauce Families & Roux Ratios](t24-the-french-sauce-families--roux-ratios.md) is the map**, including the flour-per-cup ratios for thin, medium and thick.

**Every sauce in the next group starts from one of those three browns**, plus wine, mustard, mushrooms or pickles. That is the whole trick, and it is why they are listed parent-first.

**Wine & brown sauces.**

**Built either on a brown base ([§4.71](471-sauce-brune-flour-based-brown-sauce--brown-sauce-1.md)–[§4.73](473-jus-lié-starch-thickened-brown-sauce--brown-sauce-3.md)) or on the wine in the pan.** For a sauce made off whatever you just seared, the formula is [§T8 Pan Sauce Formula](t8-pan-sauce-formula.md).

**Butter & emulsion sauces.**

**🔴 Two of these break on you.** Hollandaise and beurre blanc are emulsions — too much heat, or butter added too fast, and they split. Everything else in this group is forgiving.

*Three more compound butters are in §4 — [§4.57 Fresh Horseradish Butter](457-fresh-horseradish-butter.md), [§4.58 Pimentón Butter](458-pimentón-butter.md) and [§4.133 Beef Butter](4133-beef-butter.md).*

**Fish & seafood sauces.**

**Cody named these too.** The Prudhomme *Sauces & Gravies* chapter is most of this group, and each one goes on far more than the single dish it was printed beside.

*[§4.38](438-mustard-sauce.md) is a second, unrelated Mustard Sauce carrying the same name.*

**Barbecue & vinegar sauces.**

**Sorted the way barbecue actually sorts itself — by what the sauce is made of, which is also by region.** Vinegar in eastern Carolina, mustard in South Carolina, tomato in Kansas City, mayonnaise in Alabama.

*The near-twins, all in §4: [§4.91](491-vinegar-sauce-eastern-north-carolina-diluted-style.md) and [§4.93](493-north-carolina-vinegar-sauce-sauces-chapter--no-tomato.md) are the other two Carolina vinegar sauces, [§4.173](4173-lexington-dip-2.md) the second Lexington dip, [§4.35](435-mustard-barbecue-sauce.md) another South Carolina mustard sauce, [§4.96](496-vinegar-based-mop-sauce.md) and [§4.119](4119-east-carolina-mop-sauce.md) two more mops, and [§4.125 Chocolate Chile](4125-chocolate-chile-barbecue-sauce.md) the outlier.*

**Fresh & cold sauces.**

**The weeknight group — nothing here needs a stove**, except the holiday row at the bottom, which is ten minutes at a boil and then cold. It is the biggest family in §4 and the most heavily curated here: where a source printed one parent plus a set of regional riffs, the parent is named and the riffs are pointed at underneath.

*The rest of this family, all in §4.* **Salsas:** [§4.46](446-tomato-pepper-salsa.md), [§4.49](449-mango-salsa.md), [§4.151](4151-meyer-lemon-salsa.md). **Herb salsas** — the four regional riffs on §4.146: [§4.147](4147-classic-french-herb-salsa.md), [§4.148](4148-mexican-ish-herb-salsa.md), [§4.149](4149-southeast-asian-ish-herb-salsa.md), [§4.150](4150-japanese-ish-herb-salsa.md), plus [§4.153](4153-indian-coconut-cilantro-chutney.md). **Chimichurri & pesto:** [§4.3](43-pesto-basil-parmesan-and-pine-nut-sauce.md), [§4.95](495-dry-chimichurri.md), [§4.130](4130-chimichurri-sauce.md), [§4.62](462-walnut-dill-pesto.md). **Vinaigrettes & dressings:** [§4.136](4136-any-other-citrus-vinaigrette.md), [§4.137](4137-tomato-vinaigrette.md), [§4.139](4139-balsamic-vinaigrette.md), [§4.140](4140-lemon-vinaigrette.md), [§4.141](4141-lime-vinaigrette.md), [§4.142](4142-rice-wine-vinaigrette.md), [§4.143](4143-miso-mustard-dressing.md). **Mayonnaise:** [§4.159](4159-rustic-mayonnaise.md), [§4.160](4160-classic-sandwich-mayo.md), [§4.162](4162-herb-mayonnaise.md). **Cold condiments:** [§4.40](440-herbed-horseradish-sauce.md), [§4.132](4132-roasted-red-pepper-and-garlic-coulis.md), and the Persian yogurts [§4.155](4155-herbed-yogurt.md)–[§4.158](4158-mast-o-laboo-persian-beet-yogurt.md). **Dipping:** [§4.42](442-asian-pear-dipping-sauce.md), [§4.175](4175-teriyaki-sauce.md), [§4.181](4181-japanese-happy-mouth-yakitori-sauce.md), [§4.182](4182-basic-pepper-paste.md), [§4.185](4185-teriyaki-brinerade-and-sauce.md), [§4.191](4191-dutch-west-indian-peanut-sauce-pindasaus.md). **Pickles & relishes:** [§4.50](450-cucumber-relish.md), [§4.51](451-shallot-marmalade.md), [§4.90](490-pickled-vegetables-encurtido.md).

**Pasta & tomato sauces.**

*The béchamel side of a pasta sauce is up in the French block — [§4.63](463-sauce-béchamel--sauce-velouté-master-white-sauce.md) and [§4.52 Balsamella](452-balsamella.md).*

**Dessert is not on this sheet.** It lives in [§14 Desserts](14-desserts.md) — 36 entries, from [Mixed Berry Cobbler](141-mixed-berry-cobbler.md) to the four pecan pies. Say the word and a dessert column gets added here.
